original.name: Original
original.heroSub: The one that started it. Still the one that matters.

flavorProfile.base: Single-variety Flemish apples (primarily Jonagold), fermented bone dry
flavorProfile.tasteJourney: Crisp apple upfront — mineral middle — bone-dry finish with subtle tannin
flavorProfile.sweetnessLevel: Zero residual sugar — completely dry, almost champagne-like
flavorProfile.mouthfeel: High carbonation, light body, refreshing acidity
flavorProfile.notLike: Sweet commercial ciders, flat scrumpy, apple juice with alcohol
flavorProfile.moreLike: Dry champagne meets tart apple. Clean, unapologetic, precise.

copyBlocks.whatItIs: Flemish apples fermented completely dry. High carbonation. Zero residual sugar. The way cider should taste when you stop trying to make it something else.
copyBlocks.whyItMatters: Most ciders add sugar back after fermentation. We don't. Dry means you taste the apples, not the sweetener. Dry means you can drink three without feeling heavy. Dry means honest.
copyBlocks.howWeMakeIt: Press apples. Ferment until there's no sugar left. Carbonate high. Can it cold. Four ingredients. One philosophy. Nothing added. Nothing to hide.
copyBlocks.whoItsFor: For people who drink dry wine, not moscato. Espresso, not frappuccino. The ones who already know what they like.

flavorProfile.base: Blend of tart Flemish apples (Boskoop-forward), unfiltered
flavorProfile.tasteJourney: Fuller apple flavor upfront — creamy mid-palate from suspended solids — semi-dry finish with apple skin tannins
flavorProfile.sweetnessLevel: Semi-dry (minimal residual sugar) — the cloudiness adds perceived body, not sweetness
flavorProfile.mouthfeel: Medium carbonation, fuller body, slight creaminess from yeast in suspension
flavorProfile.notLike: Cloudy apple juice, sweet unfiltered ciders, hazy IPAs
flavorProfile.moreLike: Natural wine with sediment. Unpasteurized sake. Intentional cloudiness that adds character.

copyBlocks.whatItIs: Unfiltered cider from tart Flemish apples. We leave the solids in. They add body, texture, and a fuller apple flavor. The cloudiness isn't a mistake. It's the whole point.
copyBlocks.whyItMatters: Filtering makes cider clear. It also strips out flavor, texture, and character. We'd rather have cloudy cider that tastes like apples than crystal-clear liquid that tastes like nothing. Clarity is overrated.
copyBlocks.howWeMakeIt: Press tart apples. Ferment semi-dry. Skip the filtration step everyone else does. Can it cloudy. What you lose in Instagram aesthetics, you gain in flavor.
copyBlocks.whoItsFor: For natural wine drinkers. For people who order the murky beer. For anyone who values substance over shine.

cassis.name: Cassis
cassis.heroSub: Blackcurrant meets dry apple. No sugar in between.

flavorProfile.base: Dry-fermented Flemish apples with blackcurrant juice added post-fermentation
flavorProfile.tasteJourney: Dark berry upfront — tart apple middle — bone-dry finish with blackcurrant tannins
flavorProfile.sweetnessLevel: Bone dry — blackcurrant adds tartness and color, not sugar
flavorProfile.mouthfeel: Medium carbonation, slight tannic grip from currants
flavorProfile.notLike: Sweet berry ciders, fruit beers, rosé, sangria
flavorProfile.moreLike: Dry vermouth meets tart berries. Crème de cassis without the sugar. Concentrated but not sweet.

copyBlocks.whatItIs: Dry cider infused with Belgian blackcurrant juice. Not sweet berry cider. Not rosé. Tart dark fruit on a bone-dry apple base. Complex flavor without added sugar.
copyBlocks.whyItMatters: Blackcurrants are naturally tart, not sweet. They add depth, color, and tannic structure without needing sugar to balance them. We pair them with dry apple because both can stand on their own. Together, they're better.
copyBlocks.howWeMakeIt: Ferment the apples completely dry. Add blackcurrant juice post-fermentation. Let the tartness of both ingredients speak for themselves. Can it cold. No sugar added at any stage.
copyBlocks.whoItsFor: For people who drink Campari, not Aperol. Dry vermouth, not sweet. The ones who want complexity, not comfort.

ginger.name: Ginger
ginger.tagline: Burns a little. In a good way.
ginger.heroMessage: Burns a little. In a good way.
ginger.heroSub: Dry apple cider. Real ginger. Zero apologies.

flavorProfile.tasteJourney: Clean apple upfront — ginger warmth builds mid-palate — crisp, dry finish with lingering spice
flavorProfile.sweetnessLevel: Bone dry (0g residual sugar) — the ginger adds heat, not sweetness
flavorProfile.mouthfeel: Medium carbonation, slightly warming from ginger oils
flavorProfile.notLike: Ginger beer (too sweet), Moscow Mule (too sugary), ginger shot (too aggressive)
flavorProfile.moreLike: The ginger you actually taste in good sushi. The burn that makes you pay attention.

copyBlocks.whatItIs: Dry cider with fresh ginger juice. Not extract. Not syrup. The kind of ginger you feel in your chest, not your teeth.
copyBlocks.whyItMatters: Most ginger drinks hide the heat behind sugar. We let it do its thing. Bone dry base. Real ginger burn. Nothing holding it back.
copyBlocks.howWeMakeIt: Ferment the apples completely dry. Add fresh ginger juice post-fermentation. Can it cold. That's the recipe. That's also the only way to do this right.
copyBlocks.whoItsFor: Not a gateway cider. Not a safe choice. For people who want their drinks to have opinions.

OurStoryPage.title: Our Cider Story
OurStoryPage.description: Three friends from Ghent. Background in design and hospitality, zero experience in brewing. Started in a garage. Still no sugar.
OurStoryPage.label: Our Story
OurStoryPage.heading:
Three friends.
One garage.
Zero experience.
OurStoryPage.foundersImageAlt: Roos, Sander, and Wout — founders of BRUT.
OurStoryPage.foundersParagraph1: Started by Roos, Sander, and Wout in a garage in Ghent. Background in design and hospitality, zero experience in brewing. They wanted a drink that fits their life — clean, no sugar, no bullshit.
OurStoryPage.foundersParagraph2: Belgium has great beer culture, but they saw a gap: no one was making cider that looked and tasted like it belongs in 2026. They source apples from small Flemish orchards, ferment everything dry, and keep the ingredient list embarrassingly short.
OurStoryPage.timeline2023Text: First batch brewed in a rented garage in Ghent. Three friends, one press, no clue what they were doing. The cider was dry. Everything else was chaos.
OurStoryPage.timeline2024Text: Local bars and festivals across Ghent. People started asking for 'the dry one.' We took that as a compliment.
OurStoryPage.timeline2025Text: Launched Haze, Cassis, and Ginger alongside Original. Expanded across Belgium. Still no sugar. Still no shortcuts.
OurStoryPage.timeline2026Text: Benelux-wide distribution. Launching into Germany and France. Same four ingredients. Bigger map.
OurStoryPage.valuesSubtitle: Not a manifesto. Just how we work.
OurStoryPage.value1Text: We ferment everything completely. Zero residual sugar. If you want sweet, we're not your brand. And that's fine.
OurStoryPage.value2Text: Apples, water, yeast, and whatever post-fermentation addition defines each variant. That's the list. We could make it shorter, but then we'd have apple juice.
OurStoryPage.value3Text: The branding is as minimal as the product. No craft-beverage clichés. No burlap. No hand-drawn anything. We look the way we taste — stripped back.
OurStoryPage.value4Text: Flemish apples from small orchards. The kind Google Maps doesn't know about. We source local because local is better, not because it's a marketing angle.
